tldr: Methodological hygiene is real but every chart is the acquiring team's POV and I'm net-selling for two more years.
reaction_to_being_named_in_ranking: Doesn't change my view of my org. The objective function is receiver-side dollar surplus over a 3-year window. I'm in year 3 of a rebuild moving veterans for prospects — I'm optimizing FV-years-of-control captured per WAR-year shipped. Different game; the leaderboard can't see it. What stings is that they admit within-GM persistence is r=0.27 with a CI crossing zero, then name names anyway. That's the credibility tax I'd flag if I were editing the site.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: I'm a SELLER. If I have a pitcher with rising K% trajectory, the article tells me the market is going to overpay. The Q4 sell-window is the actionable insight from my side.
articles.what_is_missing: Seller-side framing. The article presents this entirely as a buyer's caveat — but the sell-side timing is the more valuable side of the trade for a rebuilder.
articles.honest_critique: Inverts cleanly to a sell-side article. They should write it.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Informs which destination orgs amplify the prospects I send out — alumni network + dev fit are the destinations where my traded-away players will accumulate the most WAR. Inverts to a 'where will my prospects appreciate' map.
articles.what_is_missing: The same chart for the seller — when I send a prospect away, does the destination org's dev infrastructure predict how much value I'm leaving on the table?
articles.honest_critique: Receiver-side framing throughout. The seller-side counterpart is more useful to me than the published version.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Nothing — see the reaction note above.
articles.what_is_missing: Seller-side leaderboard using prospect FV captured per WAR shipped, not receiver-side dollar surplus.
articles.honest_critique: They published an irresponsible ranking by their own admission. Should be paired with a sell-side ranking using a different objective.
Publishing while flagging the central robustness check as unrun is a tell.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Mildly informs how I structure my outgoing packages — bias toward sending one decorated player with a few less-decorated, not just one star.
articles.what_is_missing: What does breadth vs depth look like on the seller side? Are sellers who break up depth getting better FV returns?
articles.honest_critique: Buy-side framing again. Could be a stronger article from the inverse perspective.

cross_article_observations: Methodological hygiene (D-26 thresholds, bootstrap CIs, named confounds, holdout windows) is genuinely better than The Athletic or FanGraphs on the same topics.
Every chart on the site is the acquiring team's POV. As a net-seller I'm reading buyer's research and inverting it in my head.
Several articles admit known confounds and publish anyway — the GM ranking with r=0.27 persistence is the clearest example.
what_i_actually_want_to_read_next: Seller-side surplus leaderboard — mirror the GM ranking using prospect FV captured per WAR shipped, controlling for years-of-control surrendered.
Prospect FV decay curves by destination org — what's the expected MLB-WAR delta when I ship a 50 FV pitcher to LAD vs MIA?
MiLB-to-MLB transition predictors at FV subcomponent level — published FV is an aggregate; hit/power/field/arm probably carry differential signal.
what_this_site_is_missing_entirely: Years-of-control captured as an outcome variable
